title: C2SaferRust: Transforming C Projects Into Safer Rust With NeuroSymbolic Techniques
technique_name: C2SaferRust (C2Rust transpilation + static-analysis-based decomposition into translation units with call-site/dataflow context + LLM translation to safe Rust + compiler/test feedback repair)
core_idea_checked: C2Rust output is split by an AST traversal into units of at most L lines, ordered by reverse topological call-graph order; each unit plus call sites or live-in/live-out variables, globals and imports is sent to gpt-4o-mini to convert to idiomatic Rust, swapped in, compiled and tested, with compiler/test feedback for up to N attempts, otherwise reverted.
gain_metric: Lines of unsafe code in the uniq program (coreutils), count
baseline_name: C2Rust transpiler output (no technique; Laertes and CROWN could not run on the coreutils benchmark)
gain_quote: the largest reduction of 28%, highlighting C2S AFER R UST’s
gain_note: Table 2a, uniq, unsafe lines 6066 -> 4397 (28%); averages over 7 coreutils programs: raw pointer declarations -25%, dereferences -22%, unsafe lines -24%, unsafe calls -8%, unsafe casts -30%. All end-to-end tests still pass. On 10 Laertes programs (no tests) vs Laertes and CROWN: aggregate win/tie/loss 39/2/9 over 5 metrics (Table 3). Single run, gpt-4o-mini, N=5 repair attempts, L=150.
effect_correctness_headline: The resulting programs still pass all test cases.
benchmarks: 7 GNU coreutils programs (split, pwd, cat, truncate, uniq, tail, head) with end-to-end tests (new benchmark); 10 of 17 Laertes benchmarks (no tests)
models: gpt-4o-mini, closed, instruct
note: Project-level C-to-Rust migration technique; it needs a C project, C2Rust and end-to-end tests, so it cannot run on function-level generation benchmarks.

title: Raw Pointer Rewriting with LLMs for Translating C to Safer Rust
technique_name: PR2: decision-tree-based prompting for raw pointer lifting and statement refactoring, with code-change-analysis-guided compilation and test-case error repair
core_idea_checked: Phase 1: decision-tree prompt picks one of six safe types (Option<Box>, Option<Vec>, Option<&mut>, Option<&>, &mut [T], &[T]) and refactors use-sites; Phase 2: up to 5 repair attempts using compiler/test errors plus diff of changed statements.
gain_metric: Number of local raw pointers eliminated across 28 projects
gain_quote: Overall, PR2 removes 2,255 raw pointers, compared to 506 by L AERTES
gain_note: Section 4.2/Table 2, gpt-4o-mini, temperature 0. Metric is a proxy for memory safety (pointer counts), not a vulnerability scanner. Correctness: compile + project tests as gate; user study on 200 sampled eliminations; 57/59 LLM-test-checked uncovered cases correct.
effect_correctness_headline: all volunteers confirmed the rewritten code preserved original semantics (200 sampled eliminations); in 59 total cases we found only 2 incorrect pointer rewrites, corresponding to a 96.61% correctness rate among inspected cases
benchmarks: 28 real-world C projects with test cases from the NOPCRAT evaluation set (437 to 136k LOC, 17 to 2,731 raw pointers)
models: gpt-4o-mini, size NR, closed, instruct (main); Claude-3.5-Sonnet, size NR, closed (top 10 projects); Deepseek-v3.2, open, instruct (top 10 projects)

title: Project-Level C-to-Rust Translation via Pointer Knowledge Graphs
technique_name: PtrTrans (C-Rust Pointer Knowledge Graph-guided project-level C-to-Rust translation: KG construction, KG-guided unit-by-unit translation in dependency order, and KG-guided incremental error correction)
core_idea_checked: Clang/Doxygen/SVF analysis builds the C-Rust Pointer KG (call/refX dependencies, pointsTo/alias/derivesFrom/Access/usedIn, rule-based owning/borrowed, mutability, nullability, lifetime); SCC-condensed topological order fixes translation units; each prompt carries KG triples and translated dependency signatures; cargo check errors are repaired up to five times with KG neighbours, otherwise stubbed.
gain_metric: Unsafe Usage Count (Cargo-geiger, total over 16 projects)
baseline_name: PR2 (LLM rewriting of c2rust output, same backbone)
gain_quote: 99.9% (from 134,185 to 85) compared with PR2 [24]
gain_note: Introduction / Table 3 totals; Crown 141,866. Lint Alert Count (R/M) also drops from 4,135 (PR2) and 6,802 (Crown) to 349. Correctness vs FLOURINE: %Equiv 81.6 vs 52.3 (<4K LoC) and 67.9 vs 14.2 (4K-15K LoC). Prompts also forbid unsafe blocks and raw pointers.

Ablation: %Equiv. rises from 59.5% (PtrTrans_PS) to 81.6% (PtrTrans) and from 50.8% (PtrTrans_EC) to 81.6%
benchmarks: 16 real-world C projects from the Crown dataset (avl, buffer, genann, quadtree, rgba, urlparser, ht, bst, json.h, libtree, binn, bzip2, heman, libzahl, lil, lodepng), up to 14,829 LOC; unit tests built with LLM-generated harnesses plus AFL++ fuzzing achieve 80.0-97.7% line coverage and 87.7-100.0% function coverage
models: ChatGPT-4o, closed, default backbone (temperature = 0); Claude-3.7-Sonnet, closed; Gemini-3-Pro, closed (both used for the generalization study)

title: ENCRUST: Encapsulated Substitution and Agentic Refinement on a Live Scaffold for Safe C-to-Rust Translation

core_idea_checked: Section 3: Phase 1 wrapper/safe-function pairs with up to five compile-test retries and snapshot rollback, TDWE pass, then Phase 2 GPT-4o agent with 17 tools handling static mut, wrapper removal, struct migration, failed functions and dead code under a two-stage build/test gate.

gain_quote: Compared with C2SaferRust, Encrust reduces raw pointer dereferences by a further 42%
gain_note: Values from Table 4 Total row (garbled column-wise extraction): C2Rust 3,471, C2SaferRust 2,716, EvoC2Rust 2,385, Encrust 1,489; (2716-1489)/2716 is about 45%, not the 42% stated in text (minor inconsistency, does not change the headline). EvoC2Rust has lower counts on some metrics but its output does not compile (0% correctness), so C2SaferRust is taken as the strongest valid baseline. Headline vs C2Rust: unsafe LoC -37.8% over 15 programs. Test-vector correctness 100% for Encrust and C2SaferRust.
effect_correctness_headline: Function compilance pass rate 96.4% (Encrust) vs 66.0% (C2SaferRust) on Coreutils; Encrust achieves 100% correctness on all seven Coreutils programs and all eight Laertes libraries (EvoC2Rust 0%)
benchmarks: 7 GNU Coreutils programs (C2SaferRust benchmark; 65,117 LoC, 1,210 functions, 63 test scripts) and 8 of 10 Laertes libraries (132,589 LoC, 1,156 functions, 1,000 AFL++ inputs each); 197,706 LoC and 2,366 functions in total
models: GPT-4o, closed, general instruct (temperature 0.0)
note: Project-level C-to-Rust migration of existing codebases; no code released (only Laertes test vectors promised).
